mentions.name: Logbook
mentions.description: Logbook is a terminal-UI note-taking harness in the vein of Claude Code and OpenAI Codex, built for capturing free-flowing thoughts. Notes are saved as markdown with metadata in a local SQLite database, and longer notes can be written by launching the default shell editor from within the tool. An LLM layer extracts useful metadata and performs local ranking/categorization, and can send notes or metadata to a provider of the user's choosing (e.g. OpenAI or OpenRouter) for enrichment or filtering. Implemented slash-commands include /related, which gathers the most relevant notes on a topic such as OAuth or MCP servers, and /gaps, which flags notes that reference terms without defining them so the user can review and add context.
mentions.problem: The author has always been a lousy notetaker whose one-off and one-liner notes were never fleshed out enough to be worth revisiting — a struggle especially for engineers sitting in meetings or ramping up on new information when starting a new job. Agent memories were rejected as a solution because they tightly couple notes to codebases or agents and have unintuitive UX.
mentions.source_excerpt: I've been working on an LLM "harness" called Logbook[0] for fun with Codex.
mentions.author: joshuawertheim
